headline: Fewer than half of older patients with metastatic lung cancer received systemic therapy, study finds
dek: Stephen V Liu highlighted JAMA Oncology work by Gerard Silvestri showing 46.8% of older patients diagnosed between 2006 and 2021 received any systemic therapy.
body:
Fewer than half of older patients with metastatic lung cancer received any systemic therapy, according to work from Gerard Silvestri in JAMA Oncology, highlighted at #MaTOSLung by thoracic oncologist Stephen V Liu.

Writing on X, Liu said the study covered 250,000 older patients with metastatic lung cancer diagnosed between 2006 and 2021. Of these, "only 46.8% received any systemic therapy", he wrote.

Liu listed the factors associated with a greater likelihood of treatment: referral to an oncologist, a low comorbidity burden, being married, and survival of 90 days.

Liu, who is Chief of Hematology and Oncology at Georgetown and MedStar Georgetown University Hospital, described the work as important. He said there are now "much more effective and well tolerated treatments for lung cancer". In his view, access needs to improve and stigma needs to be overcome, so that everyone has a chance to benefit from the progress of recent years.
